about.title: Personal Injury Help in Hidden Hills, California
about.longDescription: Hidden Hills is a small, gated community of under 2,000 residents, and its equestrian-friendly streets — Jed Smith Road, El Dorado Meadow Road, Eldorado Meadow Road, and Lewis and Clark Road — see the most reported collision activity in town, based on public traffic records. The most recent finalized year on record shows zero injury collisions, zero people injured, and zero traffic deaths within city limits, though residents also travel through neighboring Los Angeles County areas where crash patterns look different. Wherever an accident happens, the aftermath is often the same: medical bills, missed work, and a lot of unanswered questions about what comes next. LawProactive is a free service that helps people in Hidden Hills connect with an independent personal injury attorney — we are not a law firm, and we don't handle your case ourselves. The attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover money on your behalf. If you or someone in your household has been hurt in a crash, fall, or other accident, reaching out costs nothing and starts the process of understanding your options under California law.

whyChoose.title: Why It Helps to Talk to an Attorney Early

items.title: The Clock on Your Claim Is Ticking
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury lawsuit, though claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can close the door on a claim entirely.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Erase Your Case
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for what happened — your share of fault simply reduces, rather than eliminates, your compensation.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain-and-Suffering Damages
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages, such as pain and suffering, in ordinary injury cases, which means an attorney can pursue what your specific situation may be worth.

items.title: You Don't Pay Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to have your case reviewed, and no attorney fee unless money is actually recovered for you.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with independent personal injury attorneys in their area. We don't represent clients ourselves or charge any fees — the attorneys we connect you with handle the legal work.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after an accident in Hidden Hills?
items.answer: In most California personal injury cases, you have two years from the date of the injury to file a lawsuit. If a government entity was involved, the deadline to file a claim can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Hidden Hills?
items.answer: Public collision records point to Jed Smith Road, El Dorado Meadow Road, Eldorado Meadow Road, and Lewis and Clark Road as the corridors with the most reported activity, with Tuesdays between 4 and 6 p.m. showing up more often than other times. These are simply counts from public records, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for my accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, so being partly responsible doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your total recovery would just be reduced by your percentage of fault, which an attorney can help assess.

items.question: Will it cost me anything to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. Connecting with an attorney through LawProactive is free, and the attorneys in our network work on contingency — meaning they only get paid if they recover money for you. There's no upfront cost or obligation to move forward.
